entry_state: Distinct accounting books preserve dated treatments rather than relabeling accounts. Customer revenue, billing, collection and advance allocation have separate state changes, including a zero-journal allocation that still needs atomic replay. The next customer-contract case must retain an obligation to refund cash after delivery.
exit_state: Customer obligations explain why identical cash can support different revenue, liabilities and future service. Costing and impairment likewise require retained histories. The equipment-preparation example has introduced separate machine, sample-production and period costs; its closing statements and depreciation remain to be read.
findings: Return estimates change revenue and recovery rights without rewriting the original estimate as an error. Separate gross assets and obligations remain visible.
The service warranty allocates 90/18 and recognizes service over supported progress. Distinct-unit modification reallocates only remaining performance; integrated modification produces a -1 catch-up.
Principal and agent cases have identical cash and profit but revenues 120 and 20. Inventory and equipment examples retain cost history. No confirmed new defect; equipment case continues next page.
